paras.en: Meeting in Toronto, the comedic pair already have signed brand collaborations with Marc Jacobs and Wildflower Cases. More recent online events from Slushy Noobz includes indie sleaze DJ livestreams with Bassvictim and a roaming “slushtruck” activation. In 2026, they took their live streams on the road to eight cities across Canada, with the uploads earned 3.2 million views across YouTube.
paras.zh: 这对喜剧组合在多伦多会面后，已经与 Marc Jacobs 和 Wildflower Cases 签署了品牌合作协议。 Slushy Noobz 最近的在线活动包括与 Bassvictim 的独立低俗 DJ 直播和漫游“slushtruck”激活。 2026 年，他们在加拿大八个城市进行了直播，上传的视频在 YouTube 上获得了 320 万次观看。

paras.en: Their podcast Out of Character has joined Will Ferrell’s Big Money Players Network, in partnership with iHeartMedia. Slushy Noobz has been profiled by Rolling Stone, Interview magazine, Wonderland, Teen Vogue, Nylon, CBC and other publications and platforms.
paras.zh: 他们的播客 Out of Character 已与 iHeartMedia 合作加入 Will Ferrell 的 Big Money Players Network。 《滚石》、《Interview》杂志、Wonderland、Teen Vogue、Nylon、CBC 等出版物和平台都对 Slushy Noobz 进行过专题报道。

paras.en: UTA launced a digital talent group in 2006 to identify and represent category-leading creators across emerging and established platforms. The UTA Creators division currently represents Jake Shane, Alix Earle, Emma Chamberlain, Keith Lee, Kareem Rahma and others.
paras.zh: UTA 于 2006 年成立了数字人才小组，旨在识别和代表新兴和成熟平台上的类别领先创作者。 UTA Creators 部门目前代表 Jake Shane、Alix Earle、Emma Chamberlain、Keith Lee、Kareem Rahma 等人。

paras.en: LASKO continues to represent Andrijasevic and Al-Emad for media relations.
paras.zh: LASKO 继续代表 Andrijasevic 和 Al-Emad 处理媒体关系。

articles.title: Trump says Nidal Hasan execution won't be livestreamed

paras.en: President Donald Trump said Thursday that the planned execution by firing squad of convicted Fort Hood mass killer Nidal Hasan would not be livestreamed, canceling the Pentagon's plans to do so.
paras.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统周四表示，行刑队计划对胡德堡大屠杀杀手尼达尔·哈桑执行死刑的行动不会进行直播，五角大楼取消了这样做的计划。

paras.en: Trump's announcement came after growing backlash against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's effort to show the former U.S. Army major's execution live online, with concern that the footage would become a recruiting tool for terrorists.
paras.zh: 特朗普宣布这一消息之前，国防部长皮特·赫格斯在网上直播这位前美国陆军少校的处决过程，遭到越来越多的强烈反对，担心这些视频会成为恐怖分子招募的工具。

paras.en: Hasan, who is paralyzed from the waist down, is scheduled to be executed Dec. 3 by an Army firing squad at 1 p.m. Central Time in Fort Hood, which is located in Killeen, Texas.
paras.zh: 哈桑腰部以下瘫痪，计划于 12 月 3 日下午 1 点被陆军行刑队处决。胡德堡中部时间，位于德克萨斯州基林。

paras.en: Hasan, who during his 2013 court-martial said he was motivated to defend the "leadership of the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan, the Taliban," could seek to delay the execution with a new legal challenge.
paras.zh: 哈桑在 2013 年军事法庭上表示，他的动机是捍卫“阿富汗伊斯兰酋长国塔利班的领导地位”，他可能会通过新的法律挑战寻求推迟处决。

paras.en: "Nidal Malik Hasan, a former U.S. Army Major turned traitor, is a very bad and evil man," Trump said in a Truth Social post. The president noted that Hasan had killed 13 people — one of whom was pregnant — and injured 32 others in the Nov. 5, 2009, shooting spree.
paras.zh: 特朗普在《真相社会》帖子中表示：“前美国陆军少校尼达尔·马利克·哈桑后来变成了叛徒，他是一个非常坏、邪恶的人。”总统指出，哈桑在 2009 年 11 月 5 日的枪击事件中杀死了 13 人，其中一人怀孕，并造成 32 人受伤。

paras.en: "With all of that being said, I think streaming the execution for all to see might have been a strong deterrent for the World to witness how America deals with Terrorists and SCUM like Hasan but, many very good and well meaning people would rather not watch him die, through streaming, or through any other visual device," Trump wrote.
paras.zh: 特朗普写道：“话虽这么说，我认为将死刑直播让所有人都能看到，可能会对世界见证美国如何处理像哈桑这样的恐怖分子和人渣有强大的威慑作用，但许多非常善良和善意的人宁愿不通过直播或任何其他视觉设备观看他的死亡。”

paras.en: "He will die, as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event will not be streamed."
paras.zh: “他将按计划被行刑队处决，但这一事件不会被直播。”

paras.en: "That said, the execution may be viewed in person by the immediate families of the victims, if they so choose," Trump wrote. "They deserve to witness JUSTICE!"
paras.zh: 特朗普写道：“也就是说，如果受害者的直系亲属愿意的话，他们可以亲自观看处决。” “他们值得见证正义！”

paras.en: Hours before Trump's announcement, a Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos poll was released and showed that 80% of Americans said the execution should not be streamed live, versus just 18% who supported the idea.
paras.zh: 在特朗普宣布这一消息之前几个小时，《华盛顿邮报》、ABC 新闻和益普索 (Ipsos) 联合发布的一项民意调查显示，80% 的美国人表示不应该现场直播执行死刑，而只有 18% 的人支持这一想法。

paras.en: About 53% of Americans support Hasan's execution, according to the poll of 2,545 U.S. adults, which had a margin of error of plus or minus two percentage points.
paras.zh: 根据对 2,545 名美国成年人的民意调查，大约 53% 的美国人支持处决哈桑，民意调查的误差幅度在正负两个百分点。

paras.en: Pentagon Spokesman Sean Parnell, in a statement to CNBC after Trump's announcement, said, "President Trump and Secretary Hegseth spoke about the decision to not livestream Hasan's execution ahead of the Truth Social announcement."
paras.zh: 五角大楼发言人肖恩·帕内尔在特朗普宣布这一消息后向 CNBC 发表声明称，“特朗普总统和赫格斯部长谈到了在真相社会宣布之前不直播哈桑处决的决定。”

paras.en: "The Secretary supports the President's decision, and they are completely aligned," Parnell said.
paras.zh: 帕内尔说：“国务卿支持总统的决定，他们的意见完全一致。”

paras.en: On Monday, Archbishop Timothy Broglio, who leads the Catholic Archdiocese for Military Services, said in a statement that any Catholics assigned to the firing squad should "request to be excused from this action contrary to the teaching of the Church."
paras.zh: 周一，负责军事服务的天主教大主教区的蒂莫西·布罗利奥大主教在一份声明中表示，任何被分配到行刑队的天主教徒都应该“请求免除这一违反教会教义的行动”。

paras.en: The Pentagon on Oct. 5 said that Trump had approved a recommendation by Hegseth to have Hasan, 56, executed by an Army firing squad.
paras.zh: 五角大楼 10 月 5 日表示，特朗普已批准赫格斯的建议，由陆军行刑队处决 56 岁的哈桑。

paras.en: Presidential approval is required for executions of military executions under the Uniform Code of Military Justice.
paras.zh: 根据《统一军事司法法典》执行军事处决需要总统批准。

paras.en: Hasan would be the first member of the U.S. military executed by firing squad since World War II. The execution also would be the first carried out by the U.S. military since 1961, when Army Pvt. John Bennett was hanged at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas, for the rape and attempted murder of a girl in Austria.
paras.zh: 哈桑将成为二战以来第一位被行刑队处决的美军成员。此次处决也将是自 1961 年以来美国军方首次执行死刑。约翰·贝内特因在奥地利强奸并企图谋杀一名女孩而在堪萨斯州莱文沃斯堡被绞死。

paras.en: Hegseth on Oct. 8 said the execution would be at Fort Hood and, "He's going to get a firing squad of soldiers, as it should be."
paras.zh: 10 月 8 日，赫格斯表示，行刑将在胡德堡进行，“他将得到一支由士兵组成的行刑队，这是应该的。”

paras.en: "And we'll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it's public, because people need to understand that ... there's serious consequences for these types of things," Hegseth said.
paras.zh: 赫格斯说：“我们将确保人们能够观看它，它是公开的，因为人们需要明白……这类事情会产生严重后果。”

paras.en: The Pentagon later said it would be livestreamed.
paras.zh: 五角大楼后来表示将进行现场直播。

paras.en: Before Trump's announcement Thursday that the livestream would not happen, it was unclear which major video-streaming platforms, if any, would have aired the execution.
paras.zh: 在特朗普周四宣布不会进行现场直播之前，尚不清楚哪些主要视频流媒体平台（如果有的话）会直播执行死刑。

paras.en: The Verge reported last week that YouTube, Twitch, Meta and X did not respond when asked if they would allow the execution on their sites, while TikTok pointed to the company's policies barring "shocking and graphic content."
paras.zh: The Verge 上周报道称，当被问及是否允许在其网站上执行死刑时，YouTube、Twitch、Meta 和 X 没有做出回应，而 TikTok 则指出该公司的政策禁止“令人震惊和血腥内容”。

paras.en: Vice President JD Vance raised doubts last week about whether the livestream is "actually going to happen," saying he would not watch it if it did.
paras.zh: 副总裁 JD Vance 上周对直播是否“真的会发生”表示怀疑，并表示如果发生的话他也不会观看。

paras.en: "So whatever the controversy is about the method of the execution, I hope that people don't forget that this is the guy who brutally murdered a lot of innocent people," Vance said. "Now, that said, if it's ultimately livestreamed, I'm not going to be watching it."
paras.zh: 万斯说：“因此，无论关于处决方式的争议如何，我希望人们不要忘记，这个人残酷地杀害了许多无辜者。” “话虽如此，如果最终直播，我就不会看。”

paras.en: Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., last week said in a post on X that the idea of livestreaming the execution was "beyond disgusting."
paras.zh: 北卡罗来纳州共和党参议员托姆·蒂利斯 (Thom Tillis) 上周在 X 上发帖称，直播死刑执行过程的想法“令人恶心”。

paras.en: "Public executions are what oppressive dictatorships like Iran and Afghanistan do," Tillis tweeted. "It should not be happening in America."
paras.zh: 蒂利斯在推特上写道：“公开处决是伊朗和阿富汗等专制独裁国家所做的事情。” “这不应该发生在美国。”

paras.en: Former Army Sgt. Alonzo Lunsford, whom Hasan shot seven times during the attack, said he opposed the execution being livestreamed even as he said he planned to attend it in person.
paras.zh: 前陆军中士。阿隆佐·伦斯福德（Alonzo Lunsford）在袭击中被哈桑开枪七次，他表示他反对现场直播行刑过程，尽管他说他计划亲自参加。

paras.en: "I want to be in the room where I can see him, and he can see me," Lunsford said last week, according to CBS News. "People have to be held accountable for their sins, but I don't want this to be some pay-per-view event, like some John Wick movie."
paras.zh: 据哥伦比亚广播公司新闻报道，伦斯福德上周表示：“我想呆在我能看到他的房间里，他也能看到我。” “人们必须为自己的罪孽负责，但我不希望这成为按次付费的活动，就像约翰威克的电影一样。”

paras.en: Archbishop Paul Coakley, president of the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops, condemned the plan to show the execution publicly.
paras.zh: 美国天主教主教会议主席保罗·科克利大主教谴责了公开展示处决的计划。

paras.en: "Our God is the God of life. In no way can [Hasan's] actions be condoned but this decision is a barbaric promotion of a culture of death and must be reconsidered. The word of God exhorts us: 'do not repay anyone evil for evil,'" Coakley said, quoting St. Paul's Letter to the Romans.
paras.zh: “我们的上帝是生命之神。哈桑的行为绝对不能得到宽恕，但这一决定是对死亡文化的野蛮宣扬，必须重新考虑。上帝的话告诫我们：‘不要以恶报恶’，”科克利引用圣保罗写给罗马人的信说。

paras.en: "The public execution even of one who has done grave harm will only further undermine the moral fabric of our nation and be a blight on the conscience of its people," Coakley said.
paras.zh: 科克利说：“即使公开处决一个造成严重伤害的人，也只会进一步破坏我们国家的道德结构，并损害人民的良心。”

paras.en: CNBC has reached out to the Pentagon for comment on Trump's post.
paras.zh: CNBC 已联系五角大楼，请其对特朗普的帖子发表评论。

paras.en: Nader Hasan, a cousin of Nidal who had spoken out after the Fort Hood shooting, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
paras.zh: 尼达尔的表弟纳德·哈桑在胡德堡枪击事件后发表了言论，他没有立即回应置评请求。

paras.en: Notre Dame Law School Professor Richard Garnett said, "The president's decision to abandon the livestreaming plan will, among other things, head off legal challenges that would likely have delayed the scheduled execution."
paras.zh: 圣母大学法学院教授理查德·加内特说：“总统放弃直播计划的决定，除其他外，将阻止可能推迟预定执行的法律挑战。”

paras.en: "As a wide range of officials and citizens have noted, a livestreamed execution would have more likely resulted in brutalization of viewers and coarsening of culture than in deterrence," Garnett said.
paras.zh: 加内特说：“正如许多官员和公民所指出的那样，现场直播的处决更有可能导致对观众的残酷对待和文化的粗俗化，而不是威慑。”

articles.title: U.S. sues California in fight over checking citizenship of mail voters

paras.en: The federal government sued the state of California on Thursday in an escalating battle over how to prevent non-U.S. citizens from voting by mail in federal elections.
paras.zh: 联邦政府周四起诉加利福尼亚州，这场争论不断升级，涉及如何阻止非美国公民在联邦选举中通过邮寄投票。

paras.en: The lawsuit asks a judge to prevent California officials from tabulating mail-in ballots "from likely non-citizens in the upcoming federal election until the voter's citizenship status can be determined."
paras.zh: 该诉讼要求法官阻止加州官员“在确定选民的公民身份之前”对即将举行的联邦选举中可能的非公民的邮寄选票进行统计。

paras.en: The Department of Justice asks that a judge order the state to set aside mail ballots from voters "identified by the Federal Government likely to be noncitizens," and to verify their citizenship status before their ballot is counted.
paras.zh: 司法部要求法官命令该州搁置“经联邦政府认定可能是非公民”的选民的邮寄选票，并在计票前核实他们的公民身份。

paras.en: The suit was filed in U.S. District Court in Los Angeles.
paras.zh: 该诉讼已向洛杉矶美国地方法院提起。

paras.en: This is breaking news. Please refresh for updates.
paras.zh: 这是突发新闻。请刷新以获取更新。

articles.title: Apple and Meta team up to make Muse AI model run on Mac computers

paras.en: Tim Cook and Mark Zuckerberg have clashed for years, but with John Ternus taking the reins at Apple, the rivals are finding common ground in artificial intelligence.
paras.zh: 蒂姆·库克（Tim Cook）和马克·扎克伯格（Mark Zuckerberg）多年来一直存在冲突，但随着约翰·特努斯（John Ternus）入主苹果，竞争对手在人工智能领域找到了共同点。

paras.en: Meta and Apple revealed a new collaboration Thursday that will enable developers to easily run Meta's new open-weight AI model on Apple's high-end desktop computers.
paras.zh: Meta 和苹果周四公布了一项新的合作，该合作将使开发人员能够在苹果的高端台式电脑上轻松运行 Meta 的新开放权重人工智能模型。

paras.en: The collaboration centers on Muse Spark Open, the most capable open-weight model released under a license that allows for limited commercial use, according to Meta. It's an 816-billion-parameter model using a so-called mixture-of-experts architecture. As an open-weight model, developers can download the technology's parameters, or weights, from the internet and run the model on a wide range of hardware.
paras.zh: 据 Meta 称，此次合作以 Muse Spark Open 为中心，这是在允许有限商业用途的许可证下发布的功能最强大的开放权重模型。它是一个包含 8160 亿个参数的模型，采用所谓的专家混合架构。作为开放权重模型，开发人员可以从互联网下载该技术的参数或权重，并在各种硬件上运行该模型。

paras.en: Customers will be able to pair between two and four Mac Studio PCs to use Muse Spark to code, analyze video or do other agentic work. The model runs locally, instead of in the cloud, adding a layer of security and saving users money, the companies said.
paras.zh: 客户将能够将两到四台 Mac Studio PC 配对，使用 Muse Spark 进行编码、分析视频或执行其他代理工作。两家公司表示，该模型在本地运行，而不是在云端运行，增加了一层安全性并为用户节省了资金。

paras.en: Thursday's announcement, following months of collaboration, is a sign that the AI boom has shifted historical alliances in Silicon Valley. For years, Apple and Meta regarded each other warily and avoided public partnerships, and the relationship hit rock bottom after Apple introduced privacy changes in 2021 that limited the targeting capabilities of digital ad companies. Meta estimated in early 2022 that the change would cut its revenue that year by $10 billion.
paras.zh: 经过数月的合作后，周四的宣布标志着人工智能的繁荣已经改变了硅谷的历史联盟。多年来，苹果和 Meta 一直对彼此保持谨慎态度，并避免公开合作，而在苹果于 2021 年推出隐私变更限制了数字广告公司的定位能力后，双方关系跌至谷底。 Meta 在 2022 年初估计，这一变化将使其当年收入减少 100 亿美元。

paras.en: Representatives from Apple and Meta declined to say if the Muse Spark Open collaboration was the start of a deeper relationship.
paras.zh: 苹果和 Meta 的代表拒绝透露 Muse Spark Open 合作是否是更深层次关系的开始。

paras.en: Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang said in an interview that many powerful open-weight models are too big to be run on the majority of personal computers, but Apple's Mac Studios make enough memory available to users so that it's practical to run Muse Spark Open.
paras.zh: Meta AI 负责人 Alexandr Wang 在接受采访时表示，许多强大的开放权重模型太大，无法在大多数个人电脑上运行，但苹果的 Mac Studio 为用户提供了足够的可用内存，因此运行 Muse Spark Open 是可行的。

paras.en: The move represents an important show of confidence in Meta's rebooted AI efforts and could pose a challenge to OpenAI and Anthropic. It could also signal Apple's growing strength in AI chips, a market that Nvidia has dominated so far due to their prevalence in large data centers.
paras.zh: 此举代表了对 Meta 重新启动的人工智能工作的信心的重要表现，并可能对 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 构成挑战。这也可能标志着苹果在人工智能芯片领域的实力不断增强，由于英伟达在大型数据中心的普及，迄今为止该市场一直由英伟达主导。

paras.en: "We worked with Apple to bring leading Agent capabilities to your desktop for the first time on the Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios, so you know we're really excited about this," Wang said. Developers can download a version of the AI model from websites like Hugging Face without extra configuration for Apple's silicon. Muse Spark Open has also been tuned to run faster on Apple's hardware, and the iPhone maker revealed new benchmarks for its chips and published technical documentation about its MLX AI framework's ability to split open-source models across multiple machines.
paras.zh: “我们与 Apple 合作，首次在 Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studio 上将领先的 Agent 功能引入您的桌面，所以您知道我们对此感到非常兴奋，”Wang 说。开发人员可以从 Hugging Face 等网站下载 AI 模型的版本，无需对苹果芯片进行额外配置。 Muse Spark Open 也经过调整，可以在苹果硬件上运行得更快，这家 iPhone 制造商公布了其芯片的新基准，并发布了有关其 MLX AI 框架在多台机器上拆分开源模型的能力的技术文档。

paras.en: Mac Studios aren't cheap though, and this AI model requires the fastest Apple chips and as much memory as possible.
paras.zh: 不过 Mac Studio 并不便宜，而且这种 AI 模型需要最快的 Apple 芯片和尽可能多的内存。

paras.en: Currently, a Mac Studio with the required M5 Ultra chip and 256GB of memory costs at least $10,799. A more expensive version with 512GB of RAM will be released later this month.
paras.zh: 目前，配备所需 M5 Ultra 芯片和 256GB 内存的 Mac Studio 售价至少为 10,799 美元。具有 512GB RAM 的更昂贵版本将于本月晚些时候发布。

paras.en: Plus, users will need to buy multiple machines.
paras.zh: 另外，用户需要购买多台机器。

paras.en: The two companies are collaborating on open-source AI, which has become a point of contention in Washington as politicians worry that free Chinese models could undercut American AI. Although Meta once centered its AI strategy on its older open-weight Llama family of models, it has since focused on creating proprietary models under the leadership of Wang, who joined Meta when the company invested more than $14 billion into his former startup Scale AI last year.
paras.zh: 两家公司正在开源人工智能方面进行合作，这已成为华盛顿的一个争论焦点，因为政界人士担心免费的中国模式可能会削弱美国的人工智能。尽管 Meta 曾经将其人工智能战略集中在其较旧的开放权重 Llama 系列模型上，但此后，它在 Wang 的领导下专注于创建专有模型。去年，当公司向他的前初创公司 Scale AI 投资超过 140 亿美元时，Wang 加入了 Meta。

paras.en: While Apple and Meta, then known as Facebook, partnered on iPhone extensions over a decade ago, they haven't struck any public partnerships since 2017 after Apple removed system-level Facebook integration from the iPhone.
paras.zh: 虽然苹果和 Meta（当时称为 Facebook）十多年前就在 iPhone 扩展方面进行了合作，但自 2017 年苹果从 iPhone 中删除系统级 Facebook 集成以来，他们就没有达成任何公共合作伙伴关系。

paras.en: "Most of the animosity predates my tenure at the company, but obviously there's been a long history between Meta and Apple," Wang said, pointing to one member of his team, AI researcher and former Apple director Daniel Gross, as a reason for the collaboration. Gross, along with former GitHub CEO Nat Friedman, was a major Zuckerberg hire last year as the Facebook founder was overhauling his company's AI strategy.
paras.zh: 王说：“大部分敌意早在我在公司任职之前就存在了，但显然 Meta 和苹果之间有着悠久的历史。”他指出，他的团队成员之一、人工智能研究员、苹果前董事丹尼尔·格罗斯 (Daniel Gross) 是这次合作的原因。去年，当 Facebook 创始人正在彻底改革公司的人工智能战略时，格罗斯和 GitHub 前首席执行官纳特·弗里德曼 (Nat Friedman) 是扎克伯格的主要雇员。

paras.en: Their leaders have also traded harsh words.
paras.zh: 他们的领导人也互相发表了严厉的言论。

paras.en: Cook, who was Apple CEO until Ternus succeeded him last month, took a shot at Zuckerberg in 2018, during the Cambridge Analytica scandal, saying, "I wouldn't be in this situation." Cook often criticized Meta for compromising user privacy.
paras.zh: 库克一直担任苹果首席执行官，直到上个月特纳斯接替他，他在 2018 年剑桥分析丑闻期间对扎克伯格进行了攻击，称“我不会陷入这种境地”。库克经常批评 Meta 损害用户隐私。

paras.en: Zuckerberg has also insulted Apple in public, telling Joe Rogan last year that the company "hasn't invented anything great since the iPhone." Zuckerberg has long sought to find a platform that Meta can own so it's not beholden to Apple.
paras.zh: 扎克伯格还曾在公开场合侮辱苹果，他去年告诉乔·罗根，该公司“自 iPhone 以来就没有发明过任何伟大的东西”。扎克伯格长期以来一直在寻求找到一个 Meta 可以拥有的平台，这样它就不会受制于苹果。

paras.en: Ternus, a hardware engineer, has already started changing things at Apple, including when it releases products.
paras.zh: 硬件工程师 Ternus 已经开始改变苹果的一切，包括在发布产品时。

paras.en: And Meta's developers haven't been able to resist Apple's products. The company bought hundreds of Mac computers so its Superintelligence team could experiment with local AI and agents earlier this year.
paras.zh: 而 Meta 的开发者一直无法抗拒苹果的产品。该公司购买了数百台 Mac 电脑，以便其超级智能团队可以在今年早些时候尝试本地人工智能和代理。

paras.en: Meta is just the latest AI model developer to team up with Apple.
paras.zh: Meta 是最新与苹果合作的人工智能模型开发商。

paras.en: In 2024, Apple announced a partnership with OpenAI to integrate ChatGPT into Siri, although the integration "dramatically underperformed" and didn't lead to OpenAI user growth, OpenAI said in a filing that's part of a legal dispute with Elon Musk's xAI. Apple sued OpenAI in July, alleging trade secret theft, a claim OpenAI denied.
paras.zh: OpenAI 在一份文件中表示，2024 年，苹果宣布与 OpenAI 合作，将 ChatGPT 集成到 Siri 中，尽管这次集成“表现明显不佳”，并且没有带来 OpenAI 用户的增长，这是与埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 的 xAI 法律纠纷的一部分。苹果公司于 7 月起诉 OpenAI，指控其窃取商业机密，但 OpenAI 否认了这一指控。

paras.en: Earlier this year, Apple announced a deal with Google, to use its Gemini models in Apple Intelligence as well as Google Cloud infrastructure.
paras.zh: 今年早些时候，苹果宣布与谷歌达成协议，在 Apple Intelligence 和谷歌云基础设施中使用其 Gemini 模型。

paras.en: Still, Apple's AI strategy has drawn criticism from investors and customers in part because its new version of Siri, released last month, isn't as advanced as chatbots and agents from leading labs.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，苹果的人工智能战略还是招致了投资者和客户的批评，部分原因是上个月发布的新版 Siri 并不像领先实验室的聊天机器人和代理那么先进。

paras.en: Meanwhile, Meta has bet big on becoming a leading lab but has struggled to keep up with the competition and its business remains almost entirely reliant on ads. Recent developments, such as Meta's Muse personal agent app and its latest proprietary foundation model, Muse Wonder, released earlier this week, have begun to excite investors who are optimistic about new AI business opportunities.
paras.zh: 与此同时，Meta 为成为领先的实验室下了很大的赌注，但一直难以跟上竞争的步伐，其业务仍然几乎完全依赖于广告。最近的发展，例如 Meta 的 Muse 个人代理应用程序及其本周早些时候发布的最新专有基础模型 Muse Wonder，已经开始让对新的人工智能商机持乐观态度的投资者兴奋不已。

paras.en: Open source remains part of Zuckerberg's AI strategy. In August, Meta debuted a small open-weight AI model dubbed Muse Glimmer, with Zuckerberg pledging to eventually release something bigger and more powerful.
paras.zh: 开源仍然是扎克伯格人工智能战略的一部分。 8 月，Meta 推出了一个名为 Muse Glimmer 的小型开放式人工智能模型，扎克伯格承诺最终会发布更大、更强大的模型。

paras.en: Muse Spark Open isn't as advanced as Muse Wonder, a proprietary offering, but Wang said it's good enough to potentially entice more coders to upgrade.
paras.zh: Muse Spark Open 不如 Muse Wonder（一种专有产品）先进，但 Wang 表示，它足以吸引更多编码人员升级。

paras.en: "These aren't the most capable models that we've developed or released," Wang said. "But we think that there will be a lot of companies and developers who sort of use this model and tinker with it at small scale and then seek to ramp up and scale up their usage."
paras.zh: “这些不是我们开发或发布的最有能力的模型，”王说。 “但我们认为会有很多公司和开发商使用这种模式并小规模地对其进行修改，然后寻求提高和扩大其使用范围。”

paras.en: WATCH: Apple makes its biggest smart-home push yet under CEO John Ternus.
paras.zh: 观看：苹果公司在首席执行官约翰·特努斯 (John Ternus) 的领导下，推出了迄今为止最大规模的智能家居业务。

articles.title: Scientists vote to end leap seconds, redefining how the world keeps time

paras.en: Today an international group of scientists, diplomats and timekeepers voted to end the leap second, which has been keeping Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) aligned with the time according to Earth’s rotation (UT1) within one second of difference. The length of a day according to UTC is close to that of UT1 but not exactly the same because our planet’s rotation is irregular. We add a leap second every few years to keep them from drifting too far apart.
paras.zh: 今天，一个由科学家、外交官和计时员组成的国际小组投票决定结束闰秒，该闰秒一直使协调世界时 (UTC) 与地球自转时间 (UT1) 保持一致，相差一秒以内。 UTC 一天的长度与 UT1 接近，但并不完全相同，因为地球的自转是不规则的。我们每隔几年添加一次闰秒，以防止它们相差太远。

paras.en: But soon the leap second will be replaced with a leap hour, added much more infrequently, which will extend the allowed difference between UT1 and UTC to an hour, or 3,600 seconds.
paras.zh: 但很快闰秒将被闰时取代，并且添加的频率要少得多，这会将 UT1 和 UTC 之间允许的差异扩大到一个小时，即 3,600 秒。

paras.en: “After 30 years of debates, we are ready,” said Noël Dimarcq, a senior scientist at the French National Center for Scientific Research (CNRS) and president of International Bureau of Weights and Measures’ (BIPM’s) Consultative Committee for Time and Frequency, just before the vote, which took place at the General Conference on Weights and Measures (CGPM) in Versailles, France.
paras.zh: “经过 30 年的争​​论，我们已经准备好了，”法国国家科学研究中心 (CNRS) 资深科学家、国际计量局 (BIPM) 时间和频率咨询委员会主席诺埃尔·迪马克 (Noël Dimarcq) 在法国凡尔赛举行的度量衡大会 (CGPM) 投票之前说道。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: UTC is the world’s standard timescale. It’s the reference for how computers, phones, boats, planes, satellites and everything else tell time and for how navigation systems such as GPS function. It’s calculated via a weighted average of the time according to atomic clocks around the world and disseminated by the BIPM.
paras.zh: UTC 是世界标准时间刻度。它是计算机、电话、船只、飞机、卫星和其他一切设备如何报时以及 GPS 等导航系统如何运行的参考。它是根据世界各地原子钟的时间加权平均值计算得出的，并由 BIPM 发布。

paras.en: Shortly after UTC was first established in 1960, scientists noticed Earth’s rotation was ever so slightly slowing down, so it was not keeping pace with the count of the seconds according to atomic clocks. At the behest of astronomers and other experts, the first leap second was added to UTC in 1972 to realign the time standard with Earth’s rotation. Since 1972, 27 leap seconds have been added.
paras.zh: 1960 年 UTC 首次建立后不久，科学家们注意到地球的自转速度稍微减慢，因此无法跟上原子钟的秒数计算。在天文学家和其他专家的要求下，UTC 于 1972 年添加了第一个闰秒，以根据地球自转重新调整时间标准。自1972年起，增加了27个闰秒。

paras.en: In the mid-2010s, however, Earth’s spin began speeding up. Scientists predicted that a negative leap second would be necessary soon, perhaps as early as 2029. Engineers say a negative leap second would be like a “mini Y2K” event because it would suddenly send the entire world one second backward in time, which could cause chaos in our digital infrastructure.
paras.zh: 然而，在 2010 年代中期，地球自转开始加速。科学家预测，负闰秒很快就会成为必要，也许最早在 2029 年。工程师表示，负闰秒就像“迷你千年虫”事件，因为它会突然使整个世界的时间倒退一秒，这可能会导致我们的数字基础设施混乱。

paras.en: “Avoiding negative leap seconds is a very big driver to open the window” between UTC and UT1, says Nick Stamatakos, head of the Earth Orientation Department at the U.S. Naval Observatory, which manages the country’s GPS grid.
paras.zh: 负责管理美国 GPS 网格的美国海军天文台地球定向部门负责人尼克·斯塔马塔科斯 (Nick Stamatakos) 表示，“避免负闰秒是打开 UTC 和 UT1 之间窗口的一个非常重要的驱动因素”。

paras.en: Since 2022 scientists, government officials, telecommunications professionals and others have been urgently trying to find a practical way to solve the leap second problem.
paras.zh: 自2022年以来，科学家、政府官员、电信专业人士和其他人士一直在紧急寻找解决闰秒问题的实用方法。

paras.en: The BIPM, which is the official source of UTC, hosts CGPM every four years to discuss issues with member states. This morning officials at this year’s conference held the vote to end the leap second and make UTC continuous, with the change taking effect on May 20 (World Metrology Day), 2027. The resolution won by a majority vote.
paras.zh: BIPM 是 UTC 的官方来源，每四年举办一次 CGPM，与成员国讨论问题。今天上午，今年会议的官员们举行了投票，决定结束闰秒并使UTC连续，这一变化将于2027年5月20日（世界计量日）生效。该决议以多数票获胜。

paras.en: Instead of using leap seconds, everyone has agreed that they will tolerate more drift between UTC and UT1 than they had in the past. And when things get really bad, we’ll add a leap hour instead. Although leap seconds have historically been added every few years, scientists predict that a leap hour won’t be needed for more than 1,000 years—effectively ending the BIPM’s procedure to link UTC with Earth’s position in the sky.
paras.zh: 每个人都同意他们将容忍 UTC 和 UT1 之间比过去更大的漂移，而不是使用闰秒。当情况变得非常糟糕时，我们会添加闰时。尽管历来每隔几年就会添加一次闰秒，但科学家预测 1000 多年之后就不再需要闰秒了，这实际上结束了 BIPM 将 UTC 与地球在天空中的位置联系起来的程序。

paras.en: The change won’t be noticed by most of us, and switching to continuous time will be easier for our digital infrastructure—there will be much less risk of bugs or service outages arising from a leap second discontinuity. But the shift means that human civilization will even further diverge from our oldest way of telling time: by looking to the sky.
paras.zh: 我们大多数人都不会注意到这种变化，而且对于我们的数字基础设施来说，切换到连续时间将会更容易——由于闰秒不连续性而引起的错误或服务中断的风险会大大降低。但这种转变意味着人类文明将进一步偏离我们最古老的计时方式：仰望天空。

articles.title: Can AI break encryption? OpenAI’s new math has cryptographers divided

paras.en: Last week OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT, dropped 722 mathematical manuscripts online in one go, every one of them penned by an artificial intelligence model unavailable to the public. The output was far from perfect: OpenAI withdrew three of the papers within a day, and mathematicians are still poring over the rest. But the scale of the research, and the incisiveness of its insights, has some worried.
paras.zh: 上周，ChatGPT 背后的公司 OpenAI 一口气在网上投放了 722 篇数学手稿，每一篇都是由公众无法获得的人工智能模型撰写的。结果远非完美：OpenAI 在一天之内撤回了三篇论文，数学家们仍在研究其余的论文。但这项研究的规模及其见解的深刻性令人担忧。

paras.en: Math powers cryptography. Every text you send and every bank log-in you submit is protected by a math problem that’s supposedly impossible to crack. The system rests on the assumption that no one will figure out how. And AI just showed it’s pretty good at math.
paras.zh: 数学为密码学提供动力。你发送的每条短信和你提交的每一次银行登录信息都受到一道数学题的保护，而这道数学题据说是不可能破解的。该系统建立在这样一个假设之上：没有人能弄清楚如何做到这一点。人工智能刚刚证明了它在数学方面非常擅长。

paras.en: That worries Matthew Green, a cryptographer at Johns Hopkins University. In a social media post a few days after OpenAI’s massive math release, he suggested there was a 15 percent chance that we could lose confidence in existing public-key encryption algorithms—which allow computers to establish secure connections and verify digital identities without first exchanging a shared secret key.
paras.zh: 这让约翰·霍普金斯大学的密码学家马修·格林感到担忧。在 OpenAI 发布大规模数学数据几天后，他在社交媒体上发帖表示，我们有 15% 的可能对现有的公钥加密算法失去信心，这种算法允许计算机在不首先交换共享密钥的情况下建立安全连接并验证数字身份。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: That confidence comes from decades of failed attempts to break those algorithms. Take elliptic curve cryptography, used across the Internet and by cryptocurrencies. Its security relies on the belief that there’s no efficient algorithm capable of reversing the mathematical operations at its core. But if AI can spot shortcuts that humans have missed, that belief could be proven wrong.
paras.zh: 这种信心来自于几十年来打破这些算法的失败尝试。以互联网和加密货币所使用的椭圆曲线加密技术为例。它的安全性依赖于这样一种信念：不存在能够逆转其核心数学运算的有效算法。但如果人工智能能够发现人类错过的捷径，那么这种信念可能被证明是错误的。

paras.en: Humans have found such shortcuts before, Green says. An algorithm called the number field sieve made it far easier to crack RSA, another widely used public-key system, when it relied on 512-bit keys. Cryptographers responded by lengthening the keys, and 2,048 bits is now considered the minimum. Another advance on that scale “could potentially seriously reduce the security level of the schemes that we standardize,” he says.
paras.zh: 格林说，人类以前就发现过这样的捷径。当 RSA（另一种广泛使用的公钥系统）依赖 512 位密钥时，一种称为数域筛的算法使得破解 RSA 变得更加容易。密码学家的应对措施是延长密钥，现在 2,048 位被认为是最小密钥。他说，这种规模的另一项进步“可能会严重降低我们标准化方案的安全级别”。

paras.en: Govind Pimpale, a research fellow at the Foundation for American Innovation, thinks AI could make the next one more likely. Public-key cryptography depends on relatively few mathematical problems, he says, each studied by a comparatively small community. Machines could throw vastly more effort at them and find flaws or faster algorithms that would let attackers work out secret keys from public ones. “Public-key cryptography is necessary for essentially all online commerce and secure messaging, so its loss would have dire consequences,” he says.
paras.zh: 美国创新基金会研究员戈文德·皮普尔 (Govind Pimpale) 认为，人工智能可以让下一个时代更有可能发生。他说，公钥密码学依赖于相对较少的数学问题，每个问题都由相对较小的社区进行研究。机器可以投入更多的精力来发现缺陷或更快的算法，让攻击者从公共密钥中找出秘密密钥。 “公钥加密技术对于所有在线商务和安全消息传递来说都是必需的，因此它的丢失将带来可怕的后果，”他说。

paras.en: Plenty of others disagree that AI will break modern encryption. Yehuda Lindell, a professor at Bar-Ilan University in Israel and head of cryptography at Coinbase, wrote on X that there is “no evidence whatsoever” of a breakthrough against the mathematical problems underlying those systems. Nor does a single one of OpenAI’s 722 papers deal with cryptography, which Dan Boneh, a professor of computer science at Stanford University, calls “a little striking.”
paras.zh: 许多人不同意人工智能将打破现代加密技术。以色列巴伊兰大学教授、Coinbase 密码学负责人 Yehuda Lindell 在 X 上写道，“没有任何证据”表明这些系统背后的数学问题取得了突破。 OpenAI 的 722 篇论文中也没有一篇涉及密码学，斯坦福大学计算机科学教授 Dan Boneh 称其“有点令人震惊”。

paras.en: Still, Green’s worry is not entirely hypothetical. In a recent preprint, Florian Tramèr, a computer scientist at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Zurich, and his colleagues—three of them at the AI company Anthropic—pitted leading AI models against 191 code-breaking challenges. “It’s pretty clear that models’ ability in cryptanalysis is growing extremely rapidly,” Tramèr says. In summer 2025 the researchers weren’t even sure AI could reproduce relatively simple attacks. Months later, the models were turning up weaknesses no one had spotted before. Anthropic has also reported that its Claude model found a substantially improved attack on HAWK, a proposed digital signature scheme designed to withstand quantum computers.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，格林的担忧并不完全是假设。在最近的预印本中，瑞士苏黎世联邦理工学院的计算机科学家 Florian Tramèr 和他的同事（其中三人来自人工智能公司 Anthropic）将领先的人工智能模型与 191 个密码破译挑战进行了比较。 “很明显，模型的密码分析能力正在极其迅速地增长，”特拉梅尔说。 2025 年夏天，研究人员甚至不确定人工智能是否可以重现相对简单的攻击。几个月后，这些模型出现了以前没有人发现的弱点。 Anthropic 还报告称，其 Claude 模型发现对 HAWK 的攻击有了显着改进，HAWK 是一种旨在抵御量子计算机的数字签名方案。

paras.en: But there’s a huge gulf between finding weaknesses in experimental cryptography and breaking the systems that secure large parts of our digital lives. “Today no currently deployed algorithm has been broken by AI,” Pimpale concedes. The bigger concern is a shortcut that cracks an entire family of mathematical problems at once, and with it every system built on them.
paras.zh: 但发现实验密码学的弱点和破坏保护我们大部分数字生活的系统之间存在巨大的鸿沟。 “目前部署的算法还没有被人工智能破解，”Pimpale 承认。更令人担忧的是，有一条捷径可以同时解决一整套数学问题，以及以此为基础构建的每个系统。

paras.en: Public-key cryptography secures the connection between your browser and the sites you visit, and it produces the digital signatures that certify a software update or a cryptocurrency transaction. Crack it, and attackers could pose as your bank or listen in on your messages. Anyone who has stockpiled encrypted traffic could go back and read it years after the senders assumed it was safe.
paras.zh: 公钥加密技术可保护您的浏览器与您访问的网站之间的连接，并生成证明软件更新或加密货币交易的数字签名。破解它，攻击者可以冒充您的银行或监听您的消息。任何储存了加密流量的人都可以在发送者认为它是安全的几年后回去阅读它。

paras.en: Even then, it wouldn’t necessarily signal disaster. Bart Preneel, a cryptography professor at the Catholic University of Leuven (KU Leuven) in Belgium, says the consequences would depend on the scale of any breakthrough. A modest mathematical advance might dent the protection offered by existing systems but not break it. Even making an attack a billion times faster might still leave it requiring more computing power than anyone could realistically muster, AI or no AI. “I think there is, at least at this moment, no real reason to panic,” he says.
paras.zh: 即便如此，这也不一定预示着灾难。比利时鲁汶天主教大学 (KU Leuven) 的密码学教授巴特·普雷内尔 (Bart Preneel) 表示，后果将取决于任何突破的规模。适度的数学进步可能会削弱现有系统提供的保护，但不会破坏它。即使攻击速度提高了十亿倍，它仍然需要比任何人实际所能调动的更多的计算能力，无论是否有人工智能。 “我认为至少目前没有真正的理由恐慌，”他说。

paras.en: Even a modest advance would necessitate a defense upgrade, and Green thinks that that could do damage of its own. “The upgrade process itself is going to be a bit of a catastrophe,” he says. “We screw up the upgrade, and we end up with something insecure accidentally.”
paras.zh: 即使是微小的进步也需要进行防御升级，格林认为这本身可能会造成损害。 “升级过程本身将是一场灾难，”他说。 “我们搞砸了升级，最终意外地遇到了不安全的情况。”

paras.en: Eyal Ronen, a researcher at Tel Aviv University, who co-authored the cryptanalysis study, is, like Preneel, cautious. AI is already very good at finding software vulnerabilities, he says, which presents a much more immediate threat than the hypothetical disappearance of encryption. And any hacker is more likely to take the easier route, such as hacking someone’s computer to steal their encryption keys, than to try breaking the mathematics protecting them.
paras.zh: 特拉维夫大学研究员埃亚尔·罗南 (Eyal Ronen) 是这项密码分析研究的合著者，他和普雷内尔一样持谨慎态度。他说，人工智能已经非常擅长发现软件漏洞，这比假设的加密消失带来了更直接的威胁。任何黑客都更有可能采取更简单的方法，例如侵入某人的计算机以窃取他们的加密密钥，而不是尝试破坏保护他们的数学原理。

paras.en: Efforts to prepare for quantum computers, another potential threat, are already forcing governments and companies to rethink their encryption. Boneh says those efforts could help if AI discovers something unexpected, although the two threats aren’t identical. HAWK, after all, was built for the quantum era, yet AI found a way to weaken it.
paras.zh: 另一个潜在威胁——量子计算机的准备工作已经迫使政府和公司重新考虑他们的加密技术。博内表示，如果人工智能发现一些意想不到的事情，这些努力可能会有所帮助，尽管这两种威胁并不相同。毕竟，HAWK 是为量子时代而设计的，但人工智能却找到了削弱它的方法。

paras.en: For now, Boneh wants something relatively straightforward from AI companies: greater transparency about what their models have tried and how often they’ve succeeded. Green agrees. “We’re getting no signal whatsoever,” he says. If the labs have pointed their models at the mathematical problems underpinning cryptography, saying so would help reassure the people responsible for securing the Internet. “Please tell us what you have discovered when you tried some cryptography questions,” Boneh says. Until someone does, nobody can say whether AI has exposed something fundamental about the mathematics we rely on—or whether it’s simply getting better at solving problems that were always solvable.
paras.zh: 目前，Boneh 希望人工智能公司提供一些相对简单的东西：关于他们的模型尝试过的内容以及成功的频率有更大的透明度。格林同意。 “我们没有收到任何信号，”他说。如果实验室将他们的模型指向密码学基础的数学问题，那么这样说将有助于安抚负责保护互联网安全的人们。 “请告诉我们你在尝试一些密码学问题时发现了什么，”博内说。在有人这样做之前，没有人能说人工智能是否揭示了我们所依赖的数学的一些基本知识，或者它是否只是在解决总是可以解决的问题方面变得更好。

articles.title: Scientists discover an ancient shipwreck dating to when the Great Pyramid was built

paras.en: They don’t make ’em like they used to. A shipwreck believed to date to the early Bronze Age has been discovered at the bottom of the Mediterranean Sea, where it has remained sitting, complete with intact cargo.
paras.zh: 他们不像以前那样做。在地中海海底发现了一艘据信可以追溯到青铜时代早期的沉船，该沉船至今仍停泊在那里，其中载有完好无损的货物。

paras.en: The small boat was first found in 2024 by scientists at Türkiye’s Akdeniz University. A blip on their sonar screen led them to the remains, which were surrounded by three stone anchors.
paras.zh: 这艘小船是土耳其阿克德尼兹大学的科学家于 2024 年首次发现的。声纳屏幕上的一个光点引导他们找到了被三个石锚包围的遗骸。

paras.en: While old shipwrecks in the area aren’t uncommon, most have dated to roughly 2,000 to 1,500 years ago, during the Roman or Byzantine eras. This ship, however, is far older, likely dating to the early Bronze Age, when the Hattian civilization was beginning to form. The scientists believe the remains are between 4,700 and 4,400 years old. That would make this the oldest shipwreck ever found, surpassing the previous contender by centuries.
paras.zh: 虽然该地区的旧沉船并不罕见，但大多数可以追溯到大约 2,000 至 1,500 年前的罗马或拜占庭时代。然而，这艘船要古老得多，很可能可以追溯到青铜时代早期，当时哈蒂安文明刚刚开始形成。科学家认为这些遗骸的年龄在 4,700 到 4,400 年间。这将使其成为迄今为止发现的最古老的沉船，比之前的竞争者好几个世纪。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Inside the ship, the archaeologists found around 18 remarkably intact, flat-bottomed containers called amphorae, which were commonly used to store and transport liquids such as olive oil and wine at the time. Some of the containers were marked with finely etched symbols, although what they mean is not yet clear.
paras.zh: 在船内，考古学家发现了大约 18 个非常完整的平底容器，称为双耳细颈瓶，当时通常用于储存和运输橄榄油和葡萄酒等液体。一些容器上刻有精细蚀刻的符号，尽管它们的含义尚不清楚。

paras.en: The unfortunate crew of the doomed vessel were likely sailing to the west when disaster struck, the researchers wrote in a study about the wreck that was published earlier this year. The area where it was found has strong currents that can be treacherous when combined with wind, they noted.
paras.zh: 研究人员在今年早些时候发表的一份关于沉船的研究中写道，灾难发生时，这艘注定失败的船只的不幸船员很可能正在向西航行。他们指出，发现它的地区有强大的水流，与风结合时可能会很危险。

paras.en: Türkiye’s culture minister Mehmet Nuri Ersoy posted a video of the underwater site on social media on Wednesday. In the post, Ersoy said the shipwreck sheds light “on the deep-rooted history of maritime trade along the Anatolian coasts.”
paras.zh: 土耳其文化部长穆罕默德·努里·埃尔索伊周三在社交媒体上发布了一段水下遗址的视频。埃尔索伊在帖子中表示，这次沉船事件揭示了“安纳托利亚沿岸根深蒂固的海上贸易历史”。

paras.en: “We continue to illuminate Anatolia’s maritime history with new discoveries, preserving our underwater cultural heritage to pass it on to future generations,” he said.
paras.zh: “我们继续用新发现阐明安纳托利亚的海洋历史，保护我们的水下文化遗产，并将其传递给子孙后代，”他说。

articles.title: Brain implants are helping people who’ve lost their voice
articles.author: Laura Sanders

paras.en: On paper, my interview with Casey Harrell looks like any other.
paras.zh: 从表面上看，我对凯西·哈雷尔的采访看起来与其他采访没什么不同。

paras.en: I ask the questions, he answers them. He tells me about his background as a climate activist, his Southern roots and his daughter, who as a preschooler loved to dress up like a cheetah and roar around the house. “My daughter was incredibly cute in her cheetah outfit,” Harrell says.
paras.zh: 我提出问题，他回答。他向我讲述了他作为气候活动家的背景、他的南方根源和他的女儿，他的女儿在学龄前时喜欢打扮得像猎豹，在房子里咆哮。 “我女儿穿着猎豹装非常可爱，”哈勒尔说。

paras.en: The transcript tells the story of our conversation. But between the lines is an entirely different story — the story of where Harrell’s words come from.
paras.zh: 文字记录讲述了我们谈话的故事。但字里行间却是一个完全不同的故事——哈雷尔的话的出处。

paras.en: Harrell started losing his ability to speak in his early 40s, nearly six years ago. He talked to me using a brain implant that can decode his words directly from his thoughts. The device, called a brain-computer interface, is experimental. But it has transformed Harrell’s life. And it could soon transform others. Advances in computing power and AI, lessons gleaned from patient experience and investments from neurotechnology companies are starting to yield real progress on brain-computer interfaces for people who can no longer talk. In other words, Harrell’s new voice might not be so singular in the future.
paras.zh: 哈勒尔在 40 岁出头的时候开始失去说话的能力，大约六年前。他使用大脑植入物与我交谈，该植入物可以直接从他的想法中解码他的话。该设备称为脑机接口，目前处于实验阶段。但这改变了哈雷尔的生活。它很快就能改变其他人。计算能力和人工智能的进步、从患者经验中汲取的经验教训以及神经技术公司的投资正在开始为无法说话的人带来脑机接口方面的真正进展。换句话说，哈雷尔的新声音未来可能不会那么独特。

paras.en: “There’s a lot of excitement and hope in the field right now,” says Matthew Willsey, a neurosurgeon and biomedical engineer at the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor, who recently implanted a new type of speech interface in a woman’s brain. For years, Willsey says, scientists didn’t know whether attempts to decode speech would be successful; now, a body of research results points clearly to yes. “They’re thinking, ‘Wow, this is actually a usable technology that addresses a real problem that people suffer from.’”
paras.zh: “现在这个领域充满了兴奋和希望，”安娜堡密歇根大学的神经外科医生和生物医学工程师马修·威尔西 (Matthew Willsey) 说，他最近在女性大脑中植入了一种新型语音接口。威尔西说，多年来，科学家们并不知道解码语音的尝试是否会成功。现在，一系列研究结果明确表明答案是肯定的。 “他们在想，‘哇，这实际上是一项可用的技术，可以解决人们所面临的实际问题。’”

paras.en: Harrell has amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, or ALS. The progressive neurodegenerative disease, which affects an estimated 35,000 people in the United States, kills nerve cells in the brain and spinal cord that control muscles. As the neural connections between Harrell’s brain and body began to falter, he gradually lost his ability to move his muscles, leaving him confined to his bed or a wheelchair. Some of those dropped signals directed the muscles in his throat and mouth, the ones that allow him to speak.
paras.zh: 哈雷尔患有肌萎缩侧索硬化症（ALS）。这种进行性神经退行性疾病影响了美国约 35,000 人，它会杀死大脑和脊髓中控制肌肉的神经细胞。随着哈雷尔大脑和身体之间的神经连接开始动摇，他逐渐失去了移动肌肉的能力，使他只能躺在床上或轮椅上。其中一些下降的信号引导他喉咙和嘴巴的肌肉，使他能够说话。

paras.en: “I began to lose my ability to talk shortly after my diagnosis in 2020,” Harrell says. After that, it was “a slow-motion car crash” as fewer and fewer people could understand him. “[My voice] is the most important thing I have lost in this whole disease,” he says.
paras.zh: “2020 年确诊后不久，我就开始失去说话的能力，”哈勒尔说。此后，就像一场“慢镜头车祸”，能够理解他的人越来越少。 “[我的声音]是我在整个疾病中失去的最重要的东西，”他说。

paras.en: In a stroke of luck, Harrell learned through a family member about a clinical trial happening at the University of California, Davis — one that attempted to restore speech with a brain-computer interface. In 2023, Harrell had four small devices implanted on the left side of his brain. These grids of electrodes reside on Harrell’s speech motor cortex, a stretch of brain along the precentral gyrus that controls the movements required for speech.
paras.zh: 幸运的是，哈勒尔通过一位家庭成员了解到加州大学戴维斯分校正在进行的一项临床试验，该试验试图通过脑机接口恢复言语。 2023年，哈雷尔的左脑植入了四个小型装置。这些电极网格位于哈雷尔的言语运动皮层上，这是沿着中央前回的大脑区域，控制言语所需的运动。

paras.en: Today, Harrell uses his system for about 10 to 14 hours daily, making him, as he puts it, “the world’s biggest power user of the brain-to-computer interface known to man.” Hard data suggest he’s right. A recent count shows that Harrell has used his system to communicate nearly 2 million words, the scientists working with him reported in June in Nature Medicine.
paras.zh: 如今，Harrell 每天使用他的系统大约 10 到 14 个小时，正如他所说，这使他成为“人类已知的脑机接口世界上最大的超级用户”。确凿的数据表明他是对的。与 Harrell 合作的科学家于 6 月在《自然·医学》杂志上报道称，最近的统计显示，Harrell 已使用他的系统传达了近 200 万个单词。

paras.en: The very existence of Harrell’s words shows it may be possible to restore speech for people with ALS, as well as for those whose speech is impaired by stroke, paralysis, cerebral palsy and Parkinson’s disease. “This kind of technology has the potential to dramatically change the conversation,” says David Brandman, a UC Davis neurosurgeon and neuroscientist who works with Harrell.
paras.zh: 哈勒尔的话的存在表明，肌萎缩侧索硬化症患者以及因中风、瘫痪、脑瘫和帕金森病而导致言语障碍的人有可能恢复言语。 “这种技术有可能极大地改变对话，”与哈雷尔一起工作的加州大学戴维斯分校神经外科医生和神经科学家戴维·布兰德曼 (David Brandman) 说。

paras.en: Harrell’s interface still has room for improvement. It’s bulky, relatively slow and limited in what sorts of nonword sounds it can decode.
paras.zh: 哈雷尔的界面仍有改进的空间。它体积庞大、速度相对较慢，并且能够解码的非单词声音种类有限。

paras.en: But it is a “beginning,” says Leigh Hochberg, a neuroscientist at Brown University who works with Harrell. “It’s still early days. There’s a lot of research to happen, and it’s going to be very exciting.” The end game, Hochberg says, is a world in which people could use a device to communicate seamlessly, quickly, clearly — and in their former voices.
paras.zh: 但这只是一个“开始”，与哈雷尔一起工作的布朗大学神经科学家利·霍赫伯格 (Leigh Hochberg) 说。 “现在还处于早期阶段。还有很多研究要做，这将非常令人兴奋。”霍赫伯格表示，最终的世界是人们可以使用设备以他们以前的声音无缝、快速、清晰地进行交流。

paras.en: Success would mean restoring more than just people’s words, Brandman says. It would mean restoring their ability to connect in all the ineffable ways that make us human. “Speech is so fundamental to who we are,” he says. “Imagine living in a world where you couldn’t tell someone you’re in pain, or you couldn’t say that you love them … It’s not hard to imagine how devastating that would be for your quality of life.”
paras.zh: 布兰德曼说，成功不仅仅意味着恢复人们的言论。这意味着恢复他们以所有使我们成为人类的不可言喻的方式进行联系的能力。 “言语对于我们是谁至关重要，”他说。 “想象一下，生活在一个你无法告诉别人你正在痛苦中，或者你无法说你爱他们的世界......不难想象这会对你的生活质量造成多大的破坏。”

paras.en: On the path to a technology that enables fast, natural speech, scientists first had to answer a more basic question: Could the brain’s electrical chatter be decoded and translated into action outside of the head?
paras.zh: 在开发一种能够实现快速、自然语音的技术的道路上，科学家们首先必须回答一个更基本的问题：大脑的电颤动能否被解码并转化为头部之外的动作？

paras.en: Nerve cells speak to each other with tiny pulses of electricity, signals that can be picked up with electrodes. The existence of this electrical language raised the tantalizing idea that electrical messages could be decoded straight from where they originate in the brain, bypassing damaged links to the rest of the body.
paras.zh: 神经细胞通过微小的电脉冲相互交流，这些信号可以用电极接收。这种电语言的存在提出了一个诱人的想法：电信息可以直接从大脑的起源处解码，绕过与身体其他部分的受损链接。

paras.en: “This has really started as early as the 1950s, the first time scientists put electrodes into brains to record neural activity,” says Sergey Stavisky, a neuroscientist and neural engineer at UC Davis. “You can record the electrical activity of brain cells or parts of the brain. And that’s really when modern neuroscience started trying to study, how does the brain compute? How does it allow us to move our muscles?”
paras.zh: 加州大学戴维斯分校的神经科学家和神经工程师谢尔盖·斯塔维斯基 (Sergey Stavisky) 表示：“这实际上早在 20 世纪 50 年代就开始了，当时科学家第一次将电极放入大脑中来记录神经活动。” “你可以记录脑细胞或大脑部分的电活动。这就是现代神经科学开始尝试研究的时候，大脑是如何计算的？它如何让我们移动我们的肌肉？”

paras.en: Figuring out how to decode simple neural commands was the first step. Animal studies paved the way, including experiments in which rhesus monkeys consciously controlled the movements of a robotic arm using only brain signals detected by implanted electrodes.
paras.zh: 第一步是弄清楚如何解码简单的神经命令。动物研究铺平了道路，其中包括恒河猴仅使用植入电极检测到的大脑信号有意识地控制机械臂运动的实验。

paras.en: The Deep End podcast explores what makes your voice yours
paras.zh: Deep End 播客探索什么让你的声音成为你的

paras.en: What if you lost your voice? Today, AI can re-create it, and brain implants can turn thoughts into speech. This season of The Deep End follows people living through these vocal transformations — and asks what these remarkable technologies can teach us about why our voices matter in the first place.
paras.zh: 如果你失声了怎么办？如今，人工智能可以重新创造它，大脑植入物可以将思想转化为语音。这一季的《The Deep End》讲述了人们经历这些声音转变的过程，并询问这些非凡的技术可以教会我们什么，让我们了解为什么我们的声音首先如此重要。

paras.en: By 2004, scientists had enough confidence in the approach to launch a clinical trial in humans called BrainGate. Researchers implanted a grid of electrodes in the brain of a paralyzed man named Matthew Nagle. A former star athlete, Nagle was able to control a computer cursor with his thoughts alone. “That was really the starting gun of the modern version of the brain-computer interface field,” Stavisky says.
paras.zh: 到 2004 年，科学家们对这种方法有足够的信心，在人体中启动了一项名为 BrainGate 的临床试验。研究人员在一位名叫马修·内格尔（Matthew Nagle）的瘫痪男子的大脑中植入了一组电极。作为一名前明星运动员，内格尔能够仅用意念控制电脑光标。 “这确实是现代脑机接口领域的发令枪，”斯塔维斯基说。

paras.en: From there, attempts to link brain activity with some physical outcome — such as moving a computer mouse, a wheelchair or a robotic arm — blossomed. Some of these efforts focused on the brain signals and regions that controlled movements of the hands and arms. Others focused on a very tricky version of the same basic problem: talking.
paras.zh: 从那时起，将大脑活动与某些身体结果（例如移动电脑鼠标、轮椅或机械臂）联系起来的尝试蓬勃发展。其中一些努力集中在控制手和手臂运动的大脑信号和区域。其他人则关注同一基本问题的一个非常棘手的版本：​​说话。

paras.en: A brain-computer interface that could detect the intention to say a word and bypass the muscles needed to say it would be a powerful workaround for people with diseases like ALS or brain injuries. And it is no small thing to people who can no longer talk. “Losing their speech is way more devastating than losing their mobility,” says Jessica Pietrowski, a speech and language pathologist at UC Davis who has worked with many such patients. “Speech is how they maintain their identity in their relationships.”
paras.zh: 脑机接口可以检测说话的意图并绕过说话所需的肌肉，这对于患有 ALS 或脑损伤等疾病的人来说将是一种强大的解决方法。对于不能说话的人来说，这可不是一件小事。 “失去言语比失去行动能力更具破坏性，”加州大学戴维斯分校的言语和语言病理学家杰西卡·彼得罗夫斯基（Jessica Pietrowski）说，她曾与许多此类患者一起工作过。 “言语是他们在人际关系中保持身份的方式。”

paras.en: Harrell emphasizes this point. “What does my voice mean to me? It means so much,” he says. “It is the ability to parent my daughter. It is the ability to connect with my wife. It is the ability to make a wry joke with my friends.”
paras.zh: 哈雷尔强调了这一点。 “我的声音对我来说意味着什么？意义重大，”他说。 “这是养育女儿的能力。这是与妻子联系的能力。这是与朋友开玩笑的能力。”

paras.en: Talking feels effortless to most of us, but just saying hello involves a sweeping array of actions — and upwards of 100 muscles. “It’s incredibly complex and intricate, and really, an incredible human feat,” Pietrowski says.
paras.zh: 对我们大多数人来说，说话并不费力，但只是打个招呼就涉及到一系列广泛的动作，并且涉及到 100 块以上的肌肉。 “这是极其复杂和错综复杂的，确实是一项令人难以置信的人类壮举，”彼得罗斯基说。

paras.en: Consider the “h” sound in “hello.” Known as a glottal fricative, it involves an orchestra of tiny movements. First, the diaphragm contracts to fill the lungs with air. Chest and abdominal muscles push air up through relaxed vocal cords and surrounding tissues. This puff of air then travels to the mouth, where lips, jaw and tongue execute complex sequences of movements that create the rest of the sound. Finally, air waves, perfectly shaped, ripple from the mouth. Then, and only then, “you have speech,” Pietrowski says.
paras.zh: 考虑“hello”中的“h”音。它被称为声门摩擦音，涉及一系列微小的运动。首先，横膈膜收缩，使肺部充满空气。胸部和腹部肌肉通过放松的声带和周围组织将空气向上推。然后这股空气进入口腔，嘴唇、下巴和舌头执行复杂的动作序列，从而产生其余的声音。最后，形状完美的气浪从口中荡漾开来。然后，也只有到那时，“你才有发言权，”彼得罗斯基说。

paras.en: But the beginnings of this nearly miraculous transformation start in the brain, where tiny electrical nerve pulses command the body to speak. In Harrell’s trial, he would attempt to speak words, prompting his motor cortex to send signals to his body. The implanted electrodes would detect the patterns and send them to a computer to interpret. With this work-around, it didn’t matter that Harrell’s muscles didn’t get the message; the computer would.
paras.zh: 但这种近乎奇迹的转变始于大脑，微小的电神经脉冲命令身体说话。在哈勒尔的审判中，他会尝试说话，促使他的运动皮层向他的身体发送信号。植入的电极会检测这些模式并将其发送到计算机进行解释。有了这个解决办法，哈雷尔的肌肉没有收到信息就没关系了；电脑会的。

paras.en: After Harrell recovered from surgery, researchers began testing the system in his home. They collected his neural data and streamed it to computers on a nearby cart, where machine learning algorithms attempted to match Harrell’s brain activity patterns to those that predictably occur with certain sounds. Called phonemes, these sound units are the building blocks of words. The algorithm assembled the phonemes into words, as it made its best guess about what Harrell was trying to say. To limit the computational power required, the algorithm used a vocabulary of just 50 words.
paras.zh: 哈雷尔从手术中康复后，研究人员开始在他家里测试该系统。他们收集了他的神经数据，并将其传输到附近推车上的计算机，其中机器学习算法试图将哈雷尔的大脑活动模式与某些声音可预测发生的活动模式相匹配。这些声音单位称为音素，是单词的组成部分。该算法将音素组装成单词，因为它对哈雷尔想说的话做出了最好的猜测。为了限制所需的计算能力，该算法仅使用 50 个单词的词汇表。

paras.en: When the system was plugged in and ready to go, scientists asked Harrell to try and say a specific, random sentence built from that library: “What good is that?”
paras.zh: 当系统接通电源并准备就绪时，科学家要求哈勒尔尝试说出从该库中构建的一个特定的、随机的句子：“那有什么好处？”

paras.en: Harrell got to work. His eyebrows shot up as he saw the words appear on a screen in front of him in response to his thoughts. The decoder worked.
paras.zh: 哈雷尔开始工作了。当他看到面前的屏幕上出现了回应他想法的文字时，他的眉毛竖了起来。解码器工作了。

paras.en: Everyone paused. Some of the researchers started to cry. Harrell and his family became emotional. Being in the room when the switch was flipped on was “incredible,” Brandman says. “The majority of my adult life was working up to that moment, and to see it come to fruition was an incredible experience. But more than that was seeing what impact it immediately had for Casey and his family.”
paras.zh: 所有人都停了下来。一些研究人员开始哭泣。哈雷尔和他的家人情绪激动。布兰德曼说，当开关打开时在房间里的感觉“令人难以置信”。 “在那一刻之前，我成年生活的大部分时间都在努力，看到它取得成果是一次令人难以置信的经历。但更重要的是看到它对凯西和他的家人立即产生的影响。”

paras.en: Harrell remembers his feelings that day, too: “Pure joy.” Even though he wasn’t choosing his words for that first test, “it was a profound moment,” he says. “The possibilities for the near future for me and the rest of humanity were overwhelming to realize.”
paras.zh: 哈雷尔也记得那天他的感受：“纯粹的快乐。”尽管他没有为第一次测试选择措辞，但“这是一个意义深远的时刻，”他说。 “对我和其他人来说，不久的将来的可能性是难以想象的。”

paras.en: The second day of testing was even more profound, but in a personal way. This time, the system’s algorithm was using a vocabulary of over 125,000 words. This would be more challenging for the decoder, but it would give Harrell more autonomy to say what he wanted.
paras.zh: 第二天的测试更加深刻，但是以个人的方式。这次，系统算法使用的词汇量超过 125,000 个单词。这对于解码器来说会更具挑战性，但它会给哈雷尔更多的自主权来说出他想要的内容。

paras.en: Harrell started the session with a joke, Hochberg recalls, along the lines of, “Is this thing on?” But his next line was a real puzzler: “I’m looking for a cheetah.”
paras.zh: 霍赫伯格回忆说，哈雷尔以一个笑话开始了会议，大意是“这东西开着了吗？”但他的下一句话却令人费解：“我在寻找一只猎豹。”

paras.en: Hochberg, who had joined remotely on a video call, was sure it was a mistake. “There’s no way that the second sentence on the second day of using a brain-to-computer interface is going to say anything about a cheetah,” Hochberg says. “That’s obviously a decoding error.”
paras.zh: 远程加入视频通话的霍赫伯格确信这是一个错误。 “使用脑机接口的第二天的第二句话不可能说任何关于猎豹的事情，”霍赫伯格说。 “这显然是一个解码错误。”

paras.en: But there was something the scientist couldn’t see. Harrell’s 4-year-old daughter had bounded into the room, dressed as a cheetah.
paras.zh: 但有些东西科学家看不到。哈雷尔 4 岁的女儿打扮成猎豹跳进房间。

paras.en: The discovery was big scientifically, but it was bigger for what it represented to Harrell. Brain technology could restore not just his words, but also the spontaneous exchanges that had once made up his everyday life.
paras.zh: 这一发现在科学上是重大的，但它对哈雷尔来说更重要。大脑技术不仅可以恢复他的言语，还可以恢复他日常生活中的自发交流。

paras.en: “It was so amazing to be able to be understood right from the get-go and to be able to talk and respond to my daughter,” Harrell says, “especially because that was lacking completely from my life.”
paras.zh: 哈勒尔说：“能够从一开始就被理解，能够与我的女儿交谈并做出回应，真是太棒了，尤其是因为我的生活完全缺乏这些。”

paras.en: Hochberg says moments like that represent the promise that brain-computer interfaces hold. “To me, seeing it work that quickly and that powerfully really, really emphasized that these are technologies that are going to be able to restore not only activities of daily living,” he says, “but they’re going to restore communication between parent and child.”
paras.zh: 霍赫伯格表示，这样的时刻代表了脑机接口的前景。 “对我来说，看到它如此迅速和强大地发挥作用，确实强调了这些技术不仅能够恢复日常生活活动，”他说，“而且还将恢复父母和孩子之间的沟通。”

paras.en: Casey Harrell’s brain-computer interface extracts neural signals from his brain and, through a few key steps, transforms them into
paras.zh: 凯西·哈勒尔的脑机接口从他的大脑中提取神经信号，并通过几个关键步骤将它们转化为

paras.en: words. Electrodes implanted in Harrell’s speech motor cortex detect neurons’ electrical signals (1), generating raw neural data (2). Advanced machine learning efforts (3) map chunks of the data to phonemes, the building blocks of words (4). Those phonemes are then assembled into sentences by a predictive language model, or LM (5), and put on a screen where they can be read or spoken.
paras.zh: 字。植入 Harrell 言语运动皮层的电极可检测神经元的电信号 (1)，生成原始神经数据 (2)。先进的机器学习工作 (3) 将数据块映射到音素，即单词的构建块 (4)。然后，这些音素通过预测语言模型或 LM (5) 组装成句子，并放在屏幕上供阅读或说出。

paras.en: Harrell uses his interface to send email and Slack messages and play Wordle with his wife and child. He uses it to work; in fact, he’s just getting started on a new climate consultancy project. Harrell’s interface has connected him to the world in a way that would have been impossible even a few years ago.
paras.zh: Harrell 使用他的界面发送电子邮件和 Slack 消息，并与妻子和孩子一起玩 Wordle。他用它来工作；事实上，他刚刚开始一个新的气候咨询项目。哈雷尔的界面将他与世界联系起来，这在几年前是不可能的。

paras.en: But the system is still a research device. And like any early design, it comes with limitations. First, it isn’t portable; Harrell has wires coming from a port that sits on the top of his head, and he can use it only at home. And it is slow by the standards of typical conversation. You can’t tell from the written transcript of our interview, but our conversations always came with built-in delays.
paras.zh: 但该系统仍然是一个研究设备。与任何早期设计一样，它也有局限性。首先，它不便于携带；哈雷尔的电线来自他头顶上的一个端口，他只能在家里使用它。按照典型对话的标准来看，它的速度很慢。你无法从我们采访的书面记录中看出，但我们的谈话总是伴随着内在的延迟。

paras.en: For example, as we chatted, we discovered that we had both worked in the same part of Washington, D.C. I asked him if he remembered his old address. The answer came some two minutes later.
paras.zh: 例如，当我们聊天时，我们发现我们都在华盛顿特区的同一地区工作。我问他是否还记得他的旧地址。大约两分钟后就有了答案。

paras.en: “I make a very simple analogy where I talk about having the brain-to-computer interface being akin to trying to catch a train, running to get the last car before it leaves the station,” Harrell says. With the current interface, “if people are patient and wait for my sentence correction, I can [catch the train and] be a part of the conversation.”
paras.zh: “我做了一个非常简单的类比，我所说的脑机接口类似于试图赶火车，在离开车站之前跑去搭乘最后一辆车，”哈勒尔说。在目前的界面下，“如果人们有耐心等待我的句子修正，我就可以[赶火车]成为对话的一部分。”

paras.en: Harrell’s system translates his neural activity into words on a screen. If he chooses to do so, he can then use a computerized voice to say the words out loud. “It is brain-to-text, and then it gets translated to the voice,” Harrell says. A brain-to-voice system, in which a person’s thoughts are translated directly into spoken words, he adds, “is the holy grail of what this will become.”
paras.zh: 哈勒尔的系统将他的神经活动转化为屏幕上的文字。如果他选择这样做，他就可以使用计算机语音大声说出这些话。 “这是大脑到文本的过程，然后被翻译成声音，”哈勒尔说。他补充道，大脑到声音的系统可以将人的思想直接翻译成口语，“这是未来的圣杯。”

paras.en: Harrell and the scientists working with him are getting closer to this very type of real-time communication. Last year in Nature, they debuted a new algorithm that attempted to turn Harrell’s brain signals straight into sounds. The results: He could speak his mind with a delay of just 10 milliseconds. That’s very close to a real-time conversation. But the sounds Harrell made were hard to understand, with just over half of them being intelligible to listeners.
paras.zh: 哈勒尔和与他一起工作的科学家们正在接近这种类型的实时通信。去年，他们在《自然》杂志上首次推出了一种新算法，试图将哈勒尔的大脑信号直接转化为声音。结果：他说出自己的想法只需要延迟 10 毫秒。这非常接近实时对话。但哈雷尔发出的声音很难理解，其中只有一半以上是听众能听懂的。

paras.en: The next generation of devices aims to do better. Willsey, the University of Michigan neurosurgeon, is working on one such device, a fully implantable array. In June, he implanted what’s called the “cortical module,” about the size of a dime, in the brain of a 68-year-old woman. Like Harrell, the woman could no longer talk in a way that most people could understand.
paras.zh: 下一代设备的目标是做得更好。密歇根大学神经外科医生威尔西正在研究一种这样的设备，即完全植入式阵列。 6 月，他在一名 68 岁女性的大脑中植入了大约一角硬币大小的“皮质模块”。和哈勒尔一样，这位女士无法再以大多数人都能理解的方式说话。

paras.en: Unlike the BrainGate system, this new device — made by Austin, Texas–based neurotechnology company Paradromics — is portable. Surgeons implanted it in a stretch of brain tissue that made up the woman’s speech motor cortex, along the precentral gyrus. The cortical module collects neural data and sends it to another device implanted in the chest called a transceiver. From there, signals shoot to a receiver on her chest, where the data gets transformed into sounds — spoken words that play out of speakers on a nearby computer.
paras.zh: 与 BrainGate 系统不同，这款新设备由德克萨斯州奥斯汀的神经技术公司 Paradromics 制造，是便携式的。外科医生将其植入到构成该女性言语运动皮层的脑组织中，沿着中央前回。皮质模块收集神经数据并将其发送到植入胸部的另一个称为收发器的设备。从那里，信号发射到她胸前的接收器，在那里数据被转换成声音——从附近计算机的扬声器中播放出来的语音。

paras.en: Paradromics’ priority is to test whether the implant is safe. If so, scientists can turn to the goal of restoring speech in real time. “The moment that you’re thinking the words, you don’t have to wait for the sentence to complete,” says Willsey, who, like Brandman, is a site investigator for the Paradromics clinical trial. “You can let the words kind of flow out as they would in a normal conversation.”
paras.zh: Paradromics 的首要任务是测试植入物是否安全。如果是这样，科学家们就可以转向实时恢复言语的目标。 “当你想到这些词的那一刻，你不必等待句子完成，”威尔西说，他和布兰德曼一样，都是 Paradromics 临床试验的现场调查员。 “你可以像在正常谈话中一样让这些话自然而然地流露出来。”

paras.en: Scientists also want to decode more than words. Qualities of voice, such as pitch, are important for marking questions, says Vikash Gilja, a Paradromics neuroscientist. Speakers can also alter or pace their conversation to show sarcasm or concern. These sounds are all made by moving muscles, Gilja says, and can therefore be decoded from the brain.
paras.zh: 科学家们想要解码的不仅仅是文字。 Paradromics 神经科学家维卡什·吉尔贾 (Vikash Gilja) 表示，音高等语音质量对于标记问题非常重要。演讲者还可以改变或调整谈话节奏以表达讽刺或担忧。吉尔贾说，这些声音都是由肌肉运动发出的，因此可以从大脑中解码。

paras.en: “Our near-term goal right now is just to restore speech,” says Paradromics neurosurgeon Stephen Ryu. “But eventually, we’re hoping that we can actually restore someone’s ability to be fully involved in a conversation, to basically decode things like their timing, their emotions, their personality.”
paras.zh: Paradromics 神经外科医生 Stephen Ryu 表示：“我们目前的近期目标只是恢复语言能力。” “但最终，我们希望我们能够真正恢复某人完全参与对话的能力，从根本上解码他们的时间、情绪和个性等事物。”

paras.en: Other researchers are trying to incorporate the gestures that many of us use to communicate.
paras.zh: 其他研究人员正在尝试将我们许多人用来交流的手势结合起来。

paras.en: “Some gestures can substitute for speech entirely, like nodding yes, shaking your head no, waving, shrugging, giving a thumbs up,” says bioengineer Samantha Brosler of the University of California, San Fransico. Gestures can also change the meaning of words; a “maybe” with a head nod is close to a yes, for instance. “I think of gestures and body movements as an additional communication channel that can work together with speech,” Brosler says.
paras.zh: 加州大学旧金山分校的生物工程师萨曼莎·布罗斯勒表示：“有些手势可以完全代替言语，比如点头、摇头、挥手、耸肩、竖起大拇指。”手势也可以改变词语的意思；例如，点头说“也许”就接近于“是”。 “我认为手势和身体动作是一种可以与语音一起使用的额外沟通渠道，”布罗斯勒说。

paras.en: In a new study, Brosler and colleagues enabled two people with paralysis who had lost their speaking ability to instead use their brain signals to control both the words and gestures of digital avatars. The advance, reported in September in Nature Neuroscience, adds to the repertoire of signals that could be decoded and turned into action.
paras.zh: 在一项新的研究中，布罗斯勒和同事让两名失去说话能力的瘫痪患者使用大脑信号来控制数字化身的言语和手势。九月《自然神经科学》杂志报道了这一进展，增加了可以解码并转化为行动的信号库。

paras.en: And as all this is happening, scientists are creating smaller, more stable types of electrodes to embed in the brain; more powerful computational algorithms to handle larger amounts of data; and better models of how those signals relate to sounds, words and gestures, Gilja says. “We can see all the pieces coming together.”
paras.zh: 随着这一切的发生，科学家们正在创造更小、更稳定的电极来嵌入大脑；更强大的计算算法来处理更大量的数据；吉尔贾说，以及这些信号如何与声音、言语和手势相关的更好模型。 “我们可以看到所有的部分都整合在一起。”

paras.en: There are many reasons to be optimistic about the future, says Brandman, who is an investigator for the clinical trial led by Paradromics. “I think I’m about five years away from being able to meet a patient with ALS and having the following conversation,” he says. “‘Ms. Smith, I’m sorry you’ve been diagnosed with ALS. I don’t have a cure for you, but I do have a device that I can implant that can help you communicate.’”
paras.zh: Paradromics 领导的临床试验的调查员布兰德曼表示，有很多理由对未来感到乐观。 “我想我大约需要五年时间才能见到 ALS 患者并进行以下对话，”他说。 “‘史密斯女士，我很抱歉你被诊断出患有 ALS。我没有治愈你的方法，但我确实有一个可以植入的设备，可以帮助你沟通。’”

paras.en: That conversation is tantalizing. But there are no guarantees that these systems will work as hoped, or that they will be widely available. Such implants would probably come with hefty price tags, invasive brain surgeries and perhaps more demand than the few capable clinicians and technologists could meet.
paras.zh: 这段对话很诱人。但无法保证这些系统能够按预期工作，或者能够广泛使用。这种植入物可能会带来高昂的价格标签、侵入性脑部手术以及可能超出少数有能力的临床医生和技术人员能够满足的需求。

paras.en: And there are underlying questions about the brain itself. One concern is that changes to the brain over time might render neural signals unreliable, especially as diseases progress. If that happens, a person’s interface might produce a scrambled message — or be left without enough neural data to decode.
paras.zh: 大脑本身也存在一些潜在的问题。一个担忧是，随着时间的推移，大脑的变化可能会使神经信号变得不可靠，尤其是随着疾病的进展。如果发生这种情况，人的界面可能会产生混乱的消息，或者没有足够的神经数据来解码。

paras.en: “These are real challenges, and the field is working on them,” Stavisky says. “But they’re not solved yet.”
paras.zh: “这些都是真正的挑战，该领域正在努力解决这些问题，”斯塔维斯基说。 “但问题还没有解决。”

paras.en: Despite these hurdles, the push for voice-restoring technology can’t come soon enough for people who have lost theirs. In September, researchers reported that the woman with the Paradromics implant had a message for them. “OK,” she used her brain-computer interface to tell researchers. “I have a lot to say.” With her system, she was able to call her grandchildren on the telephone.
paras.zh: 尽管存在这些障碍，但对于失去声音的人来说，恢复声音技术的进展还不够快。 9 月，研究人员报告称，植入 Paradromics 的女性向他们传达了一条信息。 “好吧，”她用脑机接口告诉研究人员。 “我有很多话要说。”有了她的系统，她就能给她的孙子们打电话。

paras.en: And Harrell is now living a life that looks very different from the one he might have imagined six years ago. Although his disease keeps him close to home, he can now share his thoughts with the world — and his family — instead of locking them away inside.
paras.zh: 哈雷尔现在过着一种与他六年前想象的生活截然不同的生活。尽管他的疾病使他不得不离家很近，但他现在可以与世界和他的家人分享他的想法，而不是把它们锁在家里。

paras.en: “The ability to scream when you are running and want to get out some stress, the ability to say sweet nothings into your partner’s ear,” Harrell says. “These are the things that life is all about, and when you are robbed of those times, you want them back at all costs. And this is why this is good enough for now.”
paras.zh: “当你跑步并想要释放一些压力时能够尖叫，能够在你的伴侣耳边说些甜言蜜语，”哈勒尔说。 “这些都是生活的全部内容，当你被剥夺了那些时光时，你会不惜一切代价想要把它们找回来。这就是为什么现在这已经足够好了。”

paras.en: But he too has a vision, a day when these devices are commonplace, “when I am one of many, instead of being one of one.”
paras.zh: 但他也有一个愿景，有一天这些设备将变得司空见惯，“当我成为众多设备中的一员，而不是其中之一。”

paras.en: For more about the human voice and to hear from Casey Harrell himself, listen to The Deep End podcast Season Two, called Talk to Me. It’s free wherever you get your podcasts.
paras.zh: 有关人类声音的更多信息以及凯西·哈雷尔本人的声音，请收听 The Deep End 播客第二季，名为“跟我说话”。无论您在何处获取播客，它都是免费的。

articles.title: A telling hole in a Neandertal bone hints at a bitter end
articles.author: Freda Kreier

paras.en: A new set of remains found in modern-day Iraq suggests that one Neandertal probably suffered a devastating blow to the face before dying at the point of a spear many years later.
paras.zh: 在现代伊拉克发现的一组新遗骸表明，一名尼安德特人可能在多年后被长矛刺中，脸部遭受毁灭性打击而死亡。

paras.en: The size and structure of a puncture wound in a shoulder blade suggest that it was made by a wooden spear shortly before or after death, researchers write October 15 in Scientific Reports. But violence isn’t all this Neandertal may have known. A shattered tooth found with the remains hints that the deceased suffered a facial injury at some point in their life. Surviving this injury indicates that Neandertals may have helped each other in times of need, the study authors speculate.
paras.zh: 研究人员在 10 月 15 日的《科学报告》中写道，肩胛骨刺伤的大小和结构表明，它是在死亡前后不久由木矛造成的。但暴力并不是尼安德特人所知道的全部。遗骸中发现的一颗破碎的牙齿表明死者在生命中的某个时刻遭受过面部伤害。研究作者推测，从这次伤害中幸存下来表明尼安德特人可能在需要时互相帮助。

paras.en: These remains with visible trauma are “super cool,” because “there’s a lot of ways to die that leave absolutely no mark on your skeleton,” says Libby Cowgill, a biological anthropologist at the University of Missouri in Columbia who wasn’t involved with the study.
paras.zh: 这些带有明显创伤的遗骸“超级酷”，因为“有很多死亡方式都不会在你的骨骼上留下任何痕迹，”哥伦比亚密苏里大学生物人类学家利比·考吉尔（Libby Cowgill）说，她没有参与这项研究。

paras.en: Neandertals were often injured throughout their lives, probably from hunting. But archaeologists have also uncovered occasional signs that Neandertals and other hominids — modern humans and their extinct cousins — were stabbing and pummeling each other, maybe even intentionally, as far back as 430,000 years ago. Signs of injuries caused by other hominids have included another Neandertal at the same Iraq site whose rib was probably stabbed.
paras.zh: 尼安德特人一生中经常受伤，可能是因为狩猎。但考古学家也偶尔发现了迹象，表明尼安德特人和其他原始人类——现代人类及其已灭绝的表亲——互相刺伤和殴打，甚至可能是故意的，早在 43 万年前。其他原始人造成的伤害迹象包括伊拉克同一地点的另一名尼安德特人，其肋骨可能被刺伤。

paras.en: During an excavation that began in 2019 at Shanidar, the famous Neandertal burial site in Iraqi Kurdistan, researchers uncovered remains from at least three previously unknown individuals. The set included ribs, hand bones, teeth and a perforated shoulder bone that probably belonged to a single individual who lived around 75,000 years ago.
paras.zh: 2019 年，研究人员在伊拉克库尔德斯坦著名的尼安德特人墓地沙尼达尔 (Shanidar) 开始挖掘工作，发现了至少三具此前不为人知的人的遗骸。该套装包括肋骨、手骨、牙齿和一块穿孔的肩骨，可能属于生活在大约 75,000 年前的一个人。

paras.en: At first, the team had no idea what caused the hole, says Emma Pomeroy, a biological anthropologist at the University of Cambridge. “It’s so round, it’s like, what is it?” she recalls thinking at the time.
paras.zh: 剑桥大学生物人类学家艾玛·波默罗伊 (Emma Pomeroy) 表示，起初，研究小组并不知道造成这个洞的原因。 “它太圆了，这是什么？”她回忆起当时的想法。

paras.en: The team removed the shoulder blade with the surrounding sediment and tested for evidence that roots or insects had damaged the fossil. But that didn’t fit the nature of the damage.
paras.zh: 研究小组移除了肩胛骨和周围的沉积物，并测试了根部或昆虫损坏化石的证据。但这不符合损害的性质。

paras.en: Instead, they found fragments of bone from the shoulder blade in the dirt that suggested it had been pierced when the individual, which the team named Shanidar A, was alive. The team also didn’t see any signs of healing around the puncture wound when they analyzed the bone under the microscope and using X-rays — suggesting that the injury had occurred around the time of death.
paras.zh: 相反，他们在泥土中发现了肩胛骨的骨头碎片，这表明肩胛骨是在这个被团队命名为沙尼达尔 A 的个体活着时被刺穿的。当研究小组在显微镜下和使用 X 射线分析骨头时，也没有看到穿刺伤口周围有任何愈合的迹象，这表明损伤发生在死亡前后。

paras.en: The next task was to find out what instrument might have caused the injury. The team compared the puncture with the fossilized remains of butchered animals found alongside human tools, as well as wounds created by archaeologists stabbing animal corpses with re-created Paleolithic weapons. Stone-tipped spears usually create a diamond-shaped hole. Wooden spears, on the other hand, tend to leave round puncture wounds.
paras.zh: 下一个任务是找出可能造成伤害的仪器。研究小组将穿刺孔与与人类工具一起发现的被屠宰动物的化石残骸，以及考古学家用重建的旧石器时代武器刺伤动物尸体所造成的伤口进行了比较。石头长矛通常会形成菱形孔。另一方面，木矛往往会留下圆形刺伤。

paras.en: The wound was “absolutely, without any question,” made by a wooden spear, says Bruno Maureille, an anthropologist at the University of Bordeaux in France who wasn’t on the study team.
paras.zh: 法国波尔多大学人类学家布鲁诺·莫雷耶（Bruno Maureille）并未参与研究小组，他说，伤口“毫无疑问”是由木矛造成的。

paras.en: The team also found a broken incisor alongside the rest of the remains. The tooth was so shattered that Shanidar A probably experienced a serious injury to their face. Tartar buildup suggests that the tooth splintered in half years before Shanidar A died, meaning they lived with their disability for a long time.
paras.zh: 研究小组还在其余遗骸旁边发现了一颗破损的门牙。牙齿被震碎，沙尼达尔 A 的脸部可能受了重伤。牙垢堆积表明，沙尼达尔·A 去世前半年，这颗牙齿就碎裂了，这意味着他们在残疾中生活了很长一段时间。

paras.en: “Given it would have affected their ability to eat, to drink — they’d have been in massive amount of pain at first — it’s likely [to] have needed some care,” Pomeroy says. That one set of remains suggest both violence and care show that Neandertal “behavior is complex,” Pomeroy says. “Like us.”
paras.zh: 波默罗伊说：“考虑到这会影响他们的饮食能力——一开始他们会感到巨大的疼痛——很可能需要一些护理。”波默罗伊说，一组遗骸表明暴力和关怀都表明尼安德特人的“行为很复杂”。 “就像我们一样。”

articles.title: Many American diets may not include enough of this essential nutrient
articles.author: Aimee Cunningham

paras.en: Grocery store shelves are bursting with fancy salts: Himalayan, kosher, sea salt and more. Considering these choices, it can be easy to forget about the public health victory found in basic, iodized table salt.
paras.zh: 杂货店的货架上摆满了各种精美的盐：喜马拉雅盐、犹太盐、海盐等等。考虑到这些选择，人们很容易忘记基本的加碘食盐在公共卫生方面取得的胜利。

paras.en: The nutrient iodine is a crucial component of thyroid hormones, necessary for fetal and early childhood brain development and health throughout life. At the start of the last century, iodine deficiency was a rampant and visible public health problem in the United States, with the telltale sign of enlarged thyroid glands, called goiters, especially prevalent in much of the north. A series of steps taken by a medical society in Michigan and U.S. salt producers brought iodized salt to tables across the country, and by the 1950s, occurrences of goiters had dropped precipitously.
paras.zh: 营养物质碘是甲状腺激素的重要组成部分，是胎儿和幼儿大脑发育以及一生健康所必需的。上世纪初，碘缺乏在美国是一个严重且明显的公共卫生问题，其明显迹象是甲状腺肿大，称为甲状腺肿，在北方大部分地区尤其普遍。密歇根州的一个医学会和美国盐生产商采取了一系列措施，将碘盐带入了全国各地的餐桌，到 20 世纪 50 年代，甲状腺肿的发病率急剧下降。

paras.en: But more recently, the United States appears to be backsliding on iodine nutrition. In 2017 and 2018, 24 percent of women and 30 percent of men, aged 14 and older, weren’t getting an adequate amount of the nutrient. That’s about twice as many as in 2001 and 2002, researchers reported in the Journal of Nutrition in 2025. Breaking the data down further, nearly half of pregnant women haven’t been getting enough iodine. The study reflects an estimated, short-term look at population iodine levels.
paras.zh: 但最近，美国在碘营养方面似乎出现了倒退。 2017 年和 2018 年，14 岁及以上的 24% 女性和 30% 男性没有获得足够的营养。研究人员在 2025 年《营养杂志》上报告称，这一数字约为 2001 年和 2002 年的两倍。进一步细分数据发现，近一半的孕妇没有摄入足够的碘。该研究反映了对人口碘水平的短期估计。

paras.en: Long-term, a consistent dearth of iodine robs the body of the ability to produce sufficient amounts of thyroid hormones. If iodine levels in the population continue to trend down, that could eventually result in more goiters and harm brain development in children.
paras.zh: 长期而言，持续缺乏碘会剥夺身体产生足够量甲状腺激素的能力。如果人口中的碘含量继续下降，最终可能会导致更多的甲状腺肿并损害儿童的大脑发育。

paras.en: “The group that has the most severe potential consequences of iodine deficiency is pregnant women,” says Elizabeth Pearce, an endocrinologist at Boston University Chobanian & Avedisian School of Medicine. “Even mild degrees of iodine deficiency in pregnancy may be associated with measurably lower IQ in children.”
paras.zh: 波士顿大学 Chobanian & Avedisian 医学院的内分泌学家 Elizabeth Pearce 说：“由于缺碘，潜在后果最严重的群体是孕妇。” “即使怀孕期间轻微缺碘也可能与儿童智商明显降低有关。”

paras.en: Yet women of reproductive age, at the U.S. population level, are on the cusp of mild iodine deficiency, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention stated in its 2026 Nutrition Report.
paras.zh: 然而，美国疾病控制与预防中心在其 2026 年营养报告中指出，美国人口中的育龄妇女正处于轻度缺碘的边缘。

paras.en: With all of the ways that diets, salt intake and noniodized options have changed over time, the importance of iodine nutrition may not be top-of-mind for the general public like it was a century ago. “Iodine deficiency is the leading cause worldwide of preventable developmental delay,” says Monica Serrano-Gonzalez, a pediatric endocrinologist at Hasbro Children’s and Brown University’s Warren Alpert Medical School in Providence, R.I. “People have kind of forgotten this is a risk.”
paras.zh: 随着时间的推移，饮食、盐摄入量和非碘选择发生了各种变化，碘营养的重要性可能不再像一个世纪前那样成为公众关注的首要问题。 “碘缺乏是全世界可预防的发育迟缓的主要原因，”孩之宝儿童医院和罗德岛州普罗维登斯布朗大学沃伦阿尔珀特医学院的儿科内分泌学家 Monica Serrano-Gonzalez 说，“人们有点忘记了这是一种风险。”

paras.en: When iodine deficiency keeps the thyroid gland from making enough hormones, the body calls for more, which stimulates and enlarges the gland. That supersized gland, called a goiter, bulges at the neck. In the United States, goiters were extremely common a century ago in the Northwest, Great Lakes and Appalachians; together, the area became known as the “goiter belt.” Iodine naturally occurs in seawater and soil. But in the noncoastal northern part of the country, soils and water sources have little iodine, so the crops produced in these inland areas lack the nutrient.
paras.zh: 当缺碘导致甲状腺无法产生足够的激素时，身体就会需要更多的激素，从而刺激并扩大腺体。那个巨大的腺体，称为甲状腺肿，在颈部凸出。在美国，一个世纪前，甲状腺肿在西北地区、五大湖区和阿巴拉契亚地区极为常见。该地区一起被称为“甲状腺肿带”。碘天然存在于海水和土壤中。但在该国北部非沿海地区，土壤和水源中的碘含量很少，因此这些内陆地区生产的农作物缺乏营养。

paras.en: An examining physician for the World War I draft reported in 1918 that 30 percent of almost 600 men from a northern Michigan county had goiters, some large enough to be disqualifying. A 1922 Michigan Department of Health study of schoolchildren in four counties revealed that close to 50 percent had goiters. “It would have been a really visible public health problem at that time,” Pearce says.
paras.zh: 1918 年，一名参加第一次世界大战征兵检查的医生报告称，密歇根州北部一个县的近 600 名男子中，有 30% 患有甲状腺肿，有些甲状腺肿大到足以取消资格。 1922 年，密歇根州卫生部对四个县的学童进行的一项研究显示，近 50% 的学童患有甲状腺肿。 “当时这将是一个非常明显的公共卫生问题，”皮尔斯说。

paras.en: In response to the state’s iodine issues, the Michigan State Medical Society recommended the addition of the nutrient to table salt. The minimal expense for iodization meant this common kitchen staple would remain affordable. Companies introduced iodized salt in Michigan in the spring of 1924. By the fall, the Morton Salt Company, a major producer, was selling iodized salt nationwide. Over time, the goiters of the “belt” dwindled.
paras.zh: 为了应对该州的碘问题，密歇根州医学会建议在食盐中添加这种营养素。碘化费用极低，这意味着这种常见的厨房主食仍然可以负担得起。 1924 年春天，密歇根州的一些公司推出了碘盐。到了秋天，主要生产商莫顿盐业公司 (Morton Salt Company) 开始在全国范围内销售碘盐。随着时间的推移，“腰带”上的甲状腺肿逐渐减少。

paras.en: Salt iodization has been linked to rising IQ in the United States. For example, for men born in areas without natural sources of iodine, there was a significant jump in World War II Air Force acceptances, based on a qualifying exam, after widespread salt iodization. The increase did not occur among men born in areas with adequate natural sources of the nutrient, researchers reported in the Journal of the European Economic Association in 2017.
paras.zh: 在美国，食盐加碘与智商上升有关。例如，根据资格考试，在盐加碘广泛之后，对于出生在没有天然碘来源的地区的男性来说，二战时期空军的录取率大幅上升。研究人员在 2017 年《欧洲经济协会杂志》上报告称，出生在天然营养来源充足地区的男性并未出现这种增加。

paras.en: Adding iodine to salt was never mandated by the U.S. government. But for a long time, the voluntary approach — combined with how most people consumed salt and other dietary habits — did the trick to get people enough iodine.
